resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination says the light was abandoned circa 1930 and its lenses removed; the Society's record gives 1950 as the year discontinued and says the current optic was removed. Both are recorded as events; the record's 1950 is kept as the Society's figure, and the nomination's 1930 may refer to the front light or to the lenses. The sources do not say which.

notes_for_editor: NO STORMS CHAPTER: no storm, wreck or rescue tied to the range light was found in the sources read, and no newspaper search was run for this station, so the chapter is omitted. DEACTIVATION: the nomination (1930, possibly the front light) and the Society's record (1950) disagree; Wikipedia gives 1950 and an automation date of 1934 with no source located, so no automation date is used. HEIGHT: the nomination gives about 100 ft to the focal plane; the Society's record gives a 95 ft tower and 105 ft focal height (the record's 29.0 m and 32.0 m); Wikipedia's infobox gives 115 ft and is not used. PAGES: the 1896-1897 and 1901 volumes have no OCR scan-page index in the corpus, so those citations are to the volume, not a page; the 1894 and 1918 entries carry scan page numbers (printed page not confirmed). A page check is needed before publication. ROSTER: rear 4 lines and front 11 lines, matched by roster.py (front by name and position at 0.00 km); Charles W. Norton and Milton A. Duffield appear on both rosters, each as printed; Laura Dickinson (acting principal keeper, rear, 1907-1908) and Minnie Hann (1916) are printed without any relationship given, and the story says so. NAMES: the nomination spells Finn's; the Society spells Finns; both are kept as printed. OPENINGS: the refuge's 2026 dates (April 19, September 20, October 17-18) are past by the accessed date; the story says to check the refuge for the next season. DATES: the task brief says today is 2026-10-22; the system clock reads 2026-10-27, and accessed dates use the clock date. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-22: footnotes 5 and 6 now carry scan pages (338 for 1896-97; 45 and 138 for 1901), confirmed with corpus.py page. The refuge's full 2026 opening list is now given (the first draft gave three dates). The front roster also prints Norton for 1919, which overlaps his rear service; the story states this. Heights are given in feet with metres. The 1894 light date is from the 1894 report (scan page 403, confirmed).
